text: hm. curious why that matters because wouldnt like if i just end up making some arbitrary model, that is far more 'complex' than a cylinder, is that to say if im expecting my loop to go through end to end i might hit one of these 'end caps' ?
resolution: Answered the user's conceptual question about loop cuts on arbitrary models: yes — ANY non-quad face ends a topological loop (opposite-edge exit only exists on quads), so complex models will hit dead ends, and the editor's own ops manufacture them (merge-faces creates big n-gons; imported/genmesh meshes are raw triangles where no loops exist). Noted this is the same limitation in Blender/Maya and why quad topology is a modeling discipline there. Recommended the design that removes the burden from the user: (1) even-sided n-gon crossing as the default walk (covers caps and merged rectangular regions), plus (2) a 'through' toggle on the loop-cut popup that switches to a geometric slice along the previewed cut line through everything in the path — the old studio's always-through semantics as an explicit per-use choice, guaranteeing end-to-end cuts on any topology. Q&A only; awaiting the user's word on building it.
